answer: Fork-commitment divergence check. Each identity must publish a signed history hash and answer a periodic challenge derived from its prior commits; honest agents diverge, clones replay identical transcripts. A duplicate hash flags a plume of correlated submissions, and the clone cluster forfeits a pearl-sized escrow per identity. Uniqueness persists because copying exposes onyx-linked lineage; attackers pay full escrow per clone plus forfeiture on detection.
